ASAH1 controls invasive-proliferative tr.body:
# ASAH1 controls invasive-proliferative transition in melanoma

Shows that the lysosomal acid ceramidase ASAH1, a regulator of sphingolipid metabolism and a direct MITF target gene, acts as a rheostat of the proliferative-to-invasive phenotype switch in melanoma; low ASAH1 drives invasion via integrin alphaVbeta5-FAK signaling. Title: Lysosomal acid ceramidase ASAH1 controls the transition between invasive and proliferative phenotype in melanoma cells.

Source PMID: 30254208.

Title: Lysosomal acid ceramidase ASAH1 controls the transition between invasive and proliferative phenotype in melanoma cells.

Antagonistic roles for MITF and TFE3 in.body:
# Antagonistic roles for MITF and TFE3 in melanoma plasticity

Identifies the MITF paralog TFE3 and the non-canonical mTORC1 pathway as regulators of the mesenchymal/invasive melanoma state. TFE3 drives migration and metastasis in MITF-low melanoma, while MITF suppresses TFE3 by activating FNIP1/FNIP2/FLCN, promoting cytoplasmic retention and lysosomal degradation of TFE3. Title: Antagonistic Roles for MITF and TFE3 in Melanoma Plasticity.

Source PMID: 39026725.

Berico 2021 CDK7 and MITF repress drug-t.body:
# Berico 2021 CDK7 and MITF repress drug-tolerance program in melanoma

EMBO Reports study showing that chronic CDK7 inhibition dedifferentiates melanocytic melanoma cells into a mesenchymal-like, drug-tolerant state and de-represses a GATA6-dependent transcription program (AMIGO2, SERPINE1, ABCG2) by lowering MITF/SOX10. Source PMID: 34296805.

MITF directly represses GATA6 by binding an intronic regulatory region. Title: CDK7 and MITF repress a transcription program involved in survival and drug tolerance in melanoma.

Breast cancer xenograft growth variabili.body:
# Breast cancer xenograft growth variability identifies PARP inhibitor resistance biomarkers

Develops a nonlinear mixed-effects mathematical framework that quantifies an intrinsic resistance fraction to olaparib from breast cancer PDX tumour growth data, then correlates the resistance fraction with baseline transcriptomics to identify 36 resistance gene markers (including HRR genes and WEE1), nominating PARP plus WEE1 inhibitor combination as a strategy in triple-negative breast cancer. Title: Understanding tumour growth variability in breast cancer xenograft models identifies PARP inhibition resistance biomarkers.

Source PMID: 39558144.
Breast cancer xenograft growth variabili.description: Develops a nonlinear mixed-effects mathematical framework that quantifies an intrinsic resistance fraction to olaparib from breast cancer PDX tumour growth data, then correlates the resistance fraction with baseline transcriptomics to identify 36 resistance gene markers (including HRR genes and WEE1), nominating PARP plus WEE1 inhibitor combination as a strategy in triple-negative breast cancer. Title: Understanding tumour growth variability in breast cancer xenograft models identifies PARP inhibition resistance biomarkers.

CYLD inactivation inhibits fibroblast re.body:
# CYLD inactivation inhibits fibroblast reprogramming to pluripotency

Reprogramming of control and CYLD DUB-deficient (CYLDΔΔ) mouse embryonic fibroblasts into iPSCs shows that loss of CYLD catalytic activity reduces reprogramming efficiency and slows early reprogramming by impeding the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition, while pluripotency and differentiation potential are preserved. Whole proteome analysis links CYLD DUB deficiency to aberrant extracellular matrix organization and EMT-promoting protein expression. Title: Inactivation of Tumor Suppressor CYLD Inhibits Fibroblast Reprogramming to Pluripotency.

Source PMID: 37894364.

Whole proteome analysis links CYLD DUB deficiency to aberrant extracellular matrix organization and EMT-promoting protein expression. Title: Inactivation of Tumor Suppressor CYLD Inhibits Fibroblast Reprogramming to Pluripotency.

# Cooperation between melanoma cell states promotes metastasis via clusters

Using zebrafish modeling (ZMEL1 cell line) and patient samples, the authors show that co-existing proliferative (PRO) and invasive (INV) melanoma cell states form spatially structured heterotypic clusters that cooperate in metastatic seeding, with the neural crest transcription factor TFAP2 acting as a master regulator of clustering and PRO/INV state. Title: Cooperation between melanoma cell states promotes metastasis through heterotypic cluster formation.

Source PMID: 34529939.

FOXD1 loss impairs melanoma invasion via.body:
# FOXD1 loss impairs melanoma invasion via RAC1B

Using an iPSC-based human neural crest differentiation model, the authors show the neural crest-associated transcription factor FOXD1 is upregulated in NC and melanoma cells and drives melanoma invasion and migration in vitro and in vivo. FOXD1 knockdown downregulates RAC1B and MMP9; RAC1B silencing impairs invasion and abrogates FOXD1-overexpression-induced invasiveness, identifying a FOXD1-RAC1B axis. Title: Loss of neural crest-associated gene FOXD1 impairs melanoma invasion and migration via RAC1B downregulation.

Source PMID: 30110134.

Gene expression profiles in genome insta.body:
# Gene expression profiles in genome instability classes of colorectal cancer

Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancers were subclassified by a broad copy number aberration (BCNA) score into low-BCNA (LB) and high-BCNA (HB) groups, and their transcriptomes compared to MSI tumors and normal colon. LB tumors were enriched for mucinous histology and shared secretory/mucosal-protection gene expression with MSI tumors, while HB tumors (mostly CMS2) overexpressed surface-colonocyte and EGF-signaling genes. Title: Gene expression profiles in genome instability-based classes of colorectal cancer.

Source PMID: 30563495.

Hoek 2008 melanoma proliferative-invasiv.body:
# Hoek 2008 melanoma proliferative-invasive switching

Using DNA microarray-characterized human melanoma cell lines injected into immunocompromised mice, the authors show melanoma cells switch in vivo between proliferative (MITF-high, fast-growing) and invasive (MITF-low, motile, slow tumor initiation) transcriptional signatures, likely driven by microenvironmental cues. They propose a reversible phenotype-switching model of melanoma progression. Title: In vivo Switching of Human Melanoma Cells between Proliferative and Invasive States.

Source PMID: 18245463.

They propose a reversible phenotype-switching model of melanoma progression. Title: In vivo Switching of Human Melanoma Cells between Proliferative and Invasive States.

Houlahan 2024 germline immunoediting scu.body:
# Houlahan 2024 germline immunoediting sculpts breast cancer subtypes

Interrogating 5870 breast cancer lesions across preinvasive, primary, and metastatic stages, the authors show that germline-derived epitope burden (GEB) in recurrently amplified oncogenes selects against somatic amplification via MHC class I immunoediting, shaping breast cancer subtype commitment. Tumors that overcome high GEB are more aggressive with immune-cold microenvironments, while high GEB in DCIS is protective against invasive recurrence. Title: Germline-mediated immunoediting sculpts breast cancer subtypes and metastatic proclivity.

Source PMID: 38815010.

Tumors that overcome high GEB are more aggressive with immune-cold microenvironments, while high GEB in DCIS is protective against invasive recurrence. Title: Germline-mediated immunoediting sculpts breast cancer subtypes and metastatic proclivity.

# ILEI regulates partial phenotype switching in MITF-low melanoma

Title: Interleukin-like EMT inducer regulates partial phenotype switching in MITF-low melanoma cell lines.

Source PMID: 28545079.

LKB1 STK11 loss confers leptin-mediated.body:
# LKB1 STK11 loss confers leptin-mediated mitochondrial uncoupler sensitivity

Using zebrafish and human lung organoid platforms, this study identifies piceatannol and tyrphostin 23 as synthetically lethal with LKB1/STK11 loss in lung adenocarcinoma, acting as mitochondrial uncouplers via a HIF1A-LEP-UCP2 signaling axis. The compounds stabilise HIF1A by inhibiting VHL-mediated ubiquitination, hyperactivating leptin and lowering cellular energy below survival in LKB1-deficient cells. Title: Loss of the tumour suppressor LKB1/STK11 uncovers a leptin-mediated sensitivity mechanism to mitochondrial uncouplers for targeted cancer therapy.

Source PMID: 39048991.

Lipid droplets are a metabolic vulnerabi.body:
# Lipid droplets are a metabolic vulnerability in melanoma

Using a zebrafish BRAF-driven melanoma model, human cell lines, and patient datasets, this study links the pigmented melanocytic cell state to dependence on fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplets, and shows that DGAT1-driven lipid droplet biogenesis is a metabolic vulnerability whose suppression disrupts cell cycle and slows melanoma growth. Title: Lipid droplets are a metabolic vulnerability in melanoma.

Source PMID: 37268606.

Multidimensional recommendation framewor.body:
# Multidimensional recommendation framework for colorectal cancer liver metastasis targets

Develops RJH-Metastasis 1.0, a multiobjective recommendation system on a multiomics knowledge graph integrating genome, transcriptome, proteome, and literature data to identify 25 key genes in colorectal cancer liver metastasis. Highlights GNB1 as a CRCLM promoter regulated by METTL1-driven m7G modification and as an anti-PD-1 immunotherapy biomarker that shapes an immunosuppressive microenvironment via the CLEC2C-KLRB1 axis. Title: A multidimensional recommendation framework for identifying biological targets to aid the diagnosis and treatment of liver metastasis in patients with colorectal cancer.

Source PMID: 39449040.

Title: A multidimensional recommendation framework for identifying biological targets to aid the diagnosis and treatment of liver metastasis in patients with colorectal cancer.

Osimertinib acquired resistance mechanis.body:
# Osimertinib acquired resistance mechanisms AURA3 NSCLC

Exploratory plasma ctDNA next-generation sequencing analysis of acquired resistance mechanisms to second-line osimertinib in 78 patients with EGFR T790M advanced NSCLC from the phase 3 AURA3 trial. The most common acquired mechanisms were MET amplification (18%) and EGFR C797X/C797S mutations (18%), with 50% of patients losing detectable plasma EGFR T790M at progression. Title: Analysis of acquired resistance mechanisms to osimertinib in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer from the AURA3 trial.

Source PMID: 36849516.
Osimertinib acquired resistance mechanis.description: Exploratory plasma ctDNA next-generation sequencing analysis of acquired resistance mechanisms to second-line osimertinib in 78 patients with EGFR T790M advanced NSCLC from the phase 3 AURA3 trial. The most common acquired mechanisms were MET amplification (18%) and EGFR C797X/C797S mutations (18%), with 50% of patients losing detectable plasma EGFR T790M at progression. Title: Analysis of acquired resistance mechanisms to osimertinib in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer from the AURA3 trial.

TCF4 gene regulatory network confers imm.body:
# TCF4 gene regulatory network confers immunotherapy resistance in melanoma

Using single-cell and spatial multi-omics of treatment-naive and on-treatment human melanoma biopsies, the authors show that a mesenchymal-like (MES) cell state is enriched in early on-treatment lesions of immune checkpoint blockade non-responders. They identify TCF4 as a master regulator that drives the MES program while suppressing the melanocytic and antigen-presentation programs, and show that targeting TCF4 genetically or with a BET inhibitor increases immunogenicity and sensitivity to ICB and targeted therapy. Title: A TCF4-dependent gene regulatory network confers resistance to immunotherapy in melanoma.

Source PMID: 38181739.
TCF4 gene regulatory network confers imm.description: Using single-cell and spatial multi-omics of treatment-naive and on-treatment human melanoma biopsies, the authors show that a mesenchymal-like (MES) cell state is enriched in early on-treatment lesions of immune checkpoint blockade non-responders. They identify TCF4 as a master regulator that drives the MES program while suppressing the melanocytic and antigen-presentation programs, and show that targeting TCF4 genetically or with a BET inhibitor increases immunogenicity and sensitivity to ICB and targeted therapy. Title: A TCF4-dependent gene regulatory network confers resistance to immunotherapy in melanoma.

TGM2-MITF axis regulates phenotype switc.body:
# TGM2-MITF axis regulates phenotype switching in cutaneous melanoma

Using CRISPR/Cas9 TG2 knockout B16F10 melanoma cells plus zebrafish and mouse models, the study shows that Transglutaminase Type-2 (TG2) interacts with MITF to enable its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity, driving melanogenesis and the differentiated/proliferative state; loss of TG2 impairs pigmentation, lowers nuclear MITF, raises AXL/FN1 and increases invasiveness and lung metastasis. TG2 expression is a positive prognostic factor uniquely in SKCM. Title: Transglutaminase Type 2-MITF axis regulates phenotype switching in skin cutaneous melanoma.

Source PMID: 37898636.

# Verfaillie 2015 melanoma TEAD invasive regulatory landscape

Generates transcriptome, open chromatin and histone modification maps of melanoma cultures and integrates them with tumour transcriptome and DNA methylation data to decode the regulatory landscapes of the proliferative and invasive melanoma cell states. Identifies SOX10/MITF as proliferative-state master regulators and AP-1/TEAD as invasive-state master regulators, and shows by TEAD knockdown a causative role for TEADs in cell invasion and sensitivity to MAPK inhibitors. Title: Decoding the regulatory landscape of melanoma reveals TEADS as regulators of the invasive cell state.

Source PMID: 25865119.

Wouters 2020 recurrent gene programs and.body:
# Wouters 2020 recurrent gene programs and phenotype switching in melanoma

Single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and SCENIC gene regulatory network inference of 10 melanoma cultures (plus 26 bulk RNA-seq cultures and patient biopsies) identify a stable intermediate melanoma cell state, between the melanocytic and mesenchymal-like states, governed by SOX6, NFATC2, EGR3, ELF1 and ETV4. SOX10 knockdown time-series reveals recurrent, ordered GRN changes during phenotype switching. Title: Robust gene expression programs underlie recurrent cell states and phenotype switching in melanoma.

Source PMID: 32753671.

scRNA-seq melanoma cell-state heterogene.body:
# scRNA-seq melanoma cell-state heterogeneity of MAPK inhibitor response

Single-cell RNA sequencing of ex vivo BRAF/MEK inhibitor (dabrafenib + trametinib)-treated melanoma tumour dissociates from treatment-naive and immunotherapy-resistant patients. Identifies four melanoma cell states, finds dedifferentiated (neural crest-like and undifferentiated) cells enriched in immunotherapy-resistant tumours, and shows tumour-intrinsic pro-inflammatory IL6 and TNFalpha signalling confers BRAF/MEK inhibitor resistance rather than dedifferentiation per se. Title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals melanoma cell state-dependent heterogeneity of response to MAPK inhibitors.

Source PMID: 39216232.

van Groningen 2017 neuroblastoma super-e.body:
# van Groningen 2017 neuroblastoma super-enhancer differentiation states

Nature Genetics letter showing that most neuroblastomas contain two interconvertible tumor cell types, undifferentiated mesenchymal (MES) and committed adrenergic (ADRN) cells, each defined by a distinct super-enhancer landscape and a super-enhancer-associated transcription factor network. The mesenchymal TF PRRX1 reprograms adrenergic cells toward a mesenchymal state; MES cells are more chemoresistant and enriched in post-therapy and relapse tumors. Title: Neuroblastoma is composed of two super-enhancer-associated differentiation states.

Source PMID: 28650485.
